## Setting and question

In 2014, the Affordable Care Act offered states the option of expanding Medicaid coverage
and opened the Marketplace for private insurance. As a result, total Medicaid spending in
expansion states increased as newly eligibles were covered.

We investigate what happened to enrollment, spending and utilization during Medicaid expansion
for Medicaid, Medicare, and private insurance across states.

## Data and design

IHME Disease Expenditure Project (DEX 2.0): state-level spending and encounters by payer
and setting, all ages, 2010--2018, fit to SHEA state expenditure. 
Uninsurance from CPS. **25 states** expanded on 1 January 2014 
and **19** that never expanded were used as controls. Later expanding
cohorts are dropped (n ≤ 3 per year).

Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021) group-time difference-in-differences. Writing
$\Delta Y_t = Y_t - Y_{2013}$, the effect in year $t$ on expansion states ($D=1$) is the
change they saw, minus the change predicted for them off the never-expanded states, given
covariates $X$ --- poverty rate, median household income, pre-expansion uninsurance, and
the shares under 18 and over 65:

```{=typst}
#block(width: 100%, above: 7mm, below: 7mm)[#set text(size: 26pt)
$ "ATT"(t) = bb(E) [Delta Y_t | D=1] - bb(E) [m_t (X) | D=1] $
$ m_t (X) = bb(E) [Delta Y_t | X, D=0] $]
```

The event-study figures plot $\mathrm{ATT}(t)$; the tables report its post-period average.

```{=typst}
#block(width: 100%, above: 7mm, below: 7mm)[#set text(size: 26pt)
$ overline("ATT") = 1/5 sum_(t=2014)^2018 "ATT"(t) $]
```

**Inference** is a multiplier bootstrap, 1,000 draws, clustered on state. **Parallel
trends** is a Wald test that $\mathrm{ATT}(t)=0$ in the placebo years 2011--2013.
**Multiplicity** is Benjamini--Hochberg across the 36 spending estimates.

## Limitations

Estimates describe 2014 expanders and non-expanders only.

**Out-of-pocket spending is not included in analysis.** Uninsured spending
and out-of-pocket deductibles or copays for the insured cannot be distinguished in DEX.

Private coverage changes cannot be attributed to individual switching.

```{=typst}
#colbreak()
```
## 1. Expansion covered the uninsured

![](figures/f1_coverage.png)

```{=typst}
#note[Teal: 2014 expanding states (n = 25). Amber: non-expanding states (n = 19).]
```

| Coverage | Effect | 95% CI | Pre-test |
|:---------|-------:|:-------|---------:|
| Medicaid  | +3.69 | [+2.27, +5.12] | 0.84 |
| Medicare  | −0.20 | [−0.54, +0.14] | 0.72 |
| Uninsured | −1.38 | [−2.48, −0.28] | 0.30 |
| Private   | −2.16 | [−3.07, −1.24] | 0.96 |

Medicaid coverage rose **3.7 points** more in expansion states. The uninsured rate fell **1.4 points** further than in control
states. Private insurance increased with the Marketplace in both settings, to a greater extent in non-expansion states.


### 2. New Medicaid enrollees had similar healthcare consumption

![](figures/f2_medicaid.png)

```{=typst}
#note[Difference-in-differences effect at each year relative to 2014, as a percentage of the pre-expansion level in expansion states. 95% intervals from multiplier bootstrap.]
```
</br>

Spending across expansion states rose **18.0%** (SE 3.9) after expansion alongside **19.9%** increased enrollment. 
Spending per enrollee was not affected: **−3.3%** (SE 4.4).

### 3. Non-significant increases in private spending

![](figures/f3_private.png)

**Private coverage rose in both groups** --- 62.9 to 64.4% in expanders, 62.6 to 66.5% in
controls. Marketplace subsidies cover 100--138% FPL in states where Medicaid does not.

Private spending per enrollee and per resident rose insignificantly in 
the four years after expansion: **4.8%** (SE 2.8) and **+1.7%** (SE 2.4) respectively. 


## 4. Nothing else moved

Medicare spending per resident **+0.4%** (SE 1.3) --- nothing, on any margin. Private
spending per resident **+1.7%** (SE 2.4).

Of the **36 spending estimates** below, three survive correction for multiple comparisons,
and all three are Medicaid spending per resident. Among the **24 non-Medicaid** estimates,
one clears 5% before correction and **none survives it**.

**Spending per resident**

| Setting | Medicaid | Medicare | Private |
|:--------|---------:|---------:|--------:|
| All care    | +18.0 (3.9) * |  +0.4 (1.3) | +1.7 (2.4) |
| Ambulatory  | +23.6 (5.8) * |  −0.9 (1.2) | +2.1 (2.4) |
| Emergency   | +21.7 (8.1)   |  +2.9 (4.9) | −0.2 (1.9) |
| Inpatient   | +22.5 (4.5) * |  +0.5 (1.4) | +1.2 (3.4) |
| Nursing     |  +2.0 (6.9)   |  +3.0 (5.6) | +4.6 (7.2) |
| Pharmacy    | +11.1 (12.8)  |  +0.8 (2.9) | +0.8 (5.2) |
